//: lib: ["ES2018"] is the floor this package actually needs, and nothing more -- no DOM, no ESNext sliver, so a consumer on std's ["ES2022", "ESNext.Disposable"] set needs no expansion. Verified by compiling one step down: ES2017 (and ES2016) fail on exactly two identifiers, both in generics.ts's Replace<T,R> -- AsyncGenerator and AsyncIterable (TS2583, 'try changing lib to es2018 or later'). Everything else here is compiler-builtin (Uppercase/Lowercase/Capitalize/Exclude/Extract/Awaited) or lib.es5 (Omit, Pick, Promise, Map, Set, WeakMap, WeakKey, Function, Date); the 0n in Falsy is a bigint LITERAL type, gated by `target` (ES2022 from the base), not by lib. DOM stays out for the same reason it does in func: MessageEvent was the only identifier that wanted it, and that arm is parked. No skipLibCheck override, unlike the .d.ts-based packages this one replaces -- every file here is a .ts holding only type declarations, so it is type-checked whatever skipLibCheck says. That is the entire reason for the file form.
